findings.issue: The product feature describes a default loss guarantee (DLG) cover of up to 10% of the total amount disbursed in each quarterly portfolio, which exceeds the RBI's cap of five per cent of the total amount disbursed out of that loan portfolio at any given time.
findings.doc_evidence: CredBridge will cover losses up to 10% of the total amount disbursed in each quarterly portfolio.
findings.fix: Reduce the DLG cover from 10% to 5% of the total amount disbursed in each quarterly portfolio to comply with RBI's cap.
findings.verifier_note: The RBI paragraph explicitly states that the total amount of DLG cover on any outstanding portfolio shall not exceed five per cent of the total amount disbursed out of that loan portfolio at any given time. The product feature describes a DLG cover of up to 10% of the total amount disbursed in each quarterly portfolio, which exceeds the RBI's cap of five per cent. Therefore, the feature violates the RBI regulation.

findings.feature: Default Loss Guarantee (3. Form of DLG)
findings.issue: The product feature states that Coastal Finance will invoke the DLG once a loan has been overdue for 180 days. However, RBI requires that the RE shall invoke DLG within a maximum overdue period of 120 days, unless the loan dues are made good by the borrower before that. The feature described clearly breaks this requirement.
findings.doc_evidence: Coastal Finance will invoke the DLG once a loan has been overdue for 18,0 days.
findings.fix: Modify the product feature to invoke DLG within 120 days of loan overdue, unless the borrower has made good the dues before that period.
findings.verifier_note: The product feature states that Coastal Finance will invoke the DLG once a loan has been overdue for 180 days, which exceeds the RBI requirement of invoking DLG within a maximum overdue period of 120 days. findings.feature: Default Loss Guarantee (5. Board policy and due diligence)
findings.issue: The product feature does not comply with the requirement to obtain adequate information to satisfy itself that the entity extending DLG would be able to honour it. Therefore, the feature fails to meet the requirement of the paragraph.

summary: The compliance review of the Partnership Term Sheet between Coastal Finance and CredBridge (DLG arrangement) identified several non-compliance issues with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) regulations. The product feature exceeds the RBI's cap on default loss guarantee (DLG) coverage, as it allows up to 10% of the total amount disbursed in each quarterly portfolio, which is higher than the permissible limit of five per cent. Additionally, the DLG invocation is triggered after 180 days of loan overdue, which is beyond the RBI's requirement of 120 days. The feature also fails to specify the timeline for DLG invocation, which is a mandatory requirement. Furthermore, the product does not provide sufficient information to verify that the entity extending DLG (CredBridge) is capable of honouring the guarantee, as it lacks details on the number of REs and portfolios against which DLG has been provided.
